scope: D031-only provisional generation contracts; they are not character approvals

vamana.identity: Vishnu as the young brahmachari Vamana, later the same Lord in Trivikrama cosmic form.
vamana.anatomy: one distinct face, two attached arms and hands, two legs and feet; natural proportions for a short youthful adult.
vamana.iconography: simple ochre or saffron brahmachari dress, sacred thread, umbrella and staff when supported by scene; no peacock feather, flute, or Krishna-only marks.
vamana.trivikrama: same face and identity cues; giant scale and one coherent stride may span realms. Keep two-arm anatomy unless a specific scene contract requires otherwise.
vamana.style: flat opaque mineral matte pigment, dark drawn contours, painted ochre ornament, no gloss or metallic reflections.

mahabali.identity: Bali, adult Asura king with one consistent face and crown.
mahabali.anatomy: ordinary human adult proportions, two attached arms and hands, two legs and feet.
mahabali.continuity: courtly crown and royal garments; change expression from confidence to humility without changing identity.

shukracharya.identity: Shukracharya, Bali’s elder teacher, distinct from Bali and other sages.
shukracharya.anatomy: one face, two attached arms and hands, two legs; ordinary elderly human proportions.
shukracharya.continuity: restrained ascetic clothing and grey or white hair; do not add unsupported eye or limb traits.

vindhyavali.identity: Vindhyavali, Bali’s adult queen, shown in stanza 5.
vindhyavali.anatomy: one face, two attached arms and hands, two legs; ordinary adult proportions.
vindhyavali.continuity: distinct face and simple royal garments; maintain an unbroken pouring action with the water vessel.

garuda.identity: Garuda, divine bird-king who binds and escorts Bali.
garuda.anatomy: one birdlike head, two attached arms and hands, two wings, two legs; rope held by connected hands.
garuda.continuity: muted ochre, brown and cream feather fields; no duplicated wings or detached hands.

prahlada.identity: Prahlada, Bali’s grandfather and devotee, appearing in stanza 9.
prahlada.anatomy: one face, two attached arms and hands, two legs; ordinary mature human proportions.
prahlada.continuity: calm elder, distinct from Shukracharya, in simple devotional garments.

jambavan.identity: Jambavan, ancient bear-like devotee named in stanza 7.
jambavan.anatomy: one bear-like face and muzzle, two attached arms and hands, two legs; hold the drum with connected hands.
jambavan.continuity: small distant figure; do not clone dancers or merge him with the celestial crowd.
